help.title: What is this list?
help.subtitle: How greylisting works and what the columns mean.
help.what: Greylisting delays mail from senders it has not seen before. The first delivery attempt is turned away, and a legitimate mail server simply tries again a few minutes later, after which the mail is accepted. Most spam senders never retry. This list shows the mails currently being held back for your addresses.
help.whitelist: If you are expecting a mail that is listed here, click "Auto Whitelist": the sender is accepted immediately and will not be delayed again. Deleting an entry only removes the record; if the sender retries, it starts over.

columns.sender: The part of the sender address before the @.
columns.domain: The part of the sender address after the @.
columns.source: The address (network prefix) of the sending mail server.
columns.recipient: The address of yours the mail was sent to.
columns.firstSeen: When the first delivery attempt arrived.
